mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notary public in the country of origin

Certificate of good standing / corporate extract for any foreign corporate shareholder

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and FINTRAC guidelines, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Canadian regulations under the Special Economic Measures Act, and relevant BC enforcement databases. Enhanced due diligence is statutorily required for politically exposed persons (PEPs), including domestic PEPs, foreign PEPs, and family members or close associates.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names in British Columbia must be composed primarily of English or French words; names using non-Latin script require a Latin-script transliteration in the NUANS report. The designated name must be distinct and not likely to deceive or cause confusion with existing registered names or trademarks.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No extension of an approved name reservation is available in British Columbia; if incorporation is not completed within the 56-day validity window, a new NUANS name search and reservation application must be filed. In the event of name rejection, submit a written reconsideration request to the BC Registrar of Companies under section 420 of the Business Corporations Act within 30 days of the rejection notice, attaching the original NUANS report, a legal argument distinguishing the proposed name from conflicting marks, and any consent letters from existing name holders.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office consisting solely of a mail-forwarding address is not permissible as the registered office. The registered office in British Columbia must be a physical street address within the province where notices and service of process can be received. A corporate services provider's physical office is acceptable provided it is not a post office box.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for this industry – estimated below 5% annual likelihood of unannounced physical inspection, unless the company triggers a FINTRAC suspicious transaction report, a provincial enforcement action, or a sanctions-related investigation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under BC Business Corporations Act

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NUANS name search and name reservation report

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for cross-border low-risk corporate incorporation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), S.B.C. 2002, c. 57 — Division 2 of Part 2 (Incorporation, ss. 27–31) and Division 1 of Part 3 (Corporate Names, ss. 36–40)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia (BC Registry Services / BC Online)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form 10-100-001) together with Notice of Articles (Form 1) and Incorporation Agreement
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; BC permits one or more no-par-value shares and imposes no escrow or capital deposit requirement. A nominal subscription of 100 common shares at CAD 1.00 per share is sufficient.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The incorporation of the Corporation under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia) is hereby ratified and approved; (2) The directors listed in the Notice of Articles accept their appointments; (3) The subscription for 100 common no-par-value shares at CAD 1.00 per share is authorized, and share certificates shall be issued upon receipt of payment; (4) The registered office and records office located at Suite 1200, 800 Burrard Street, Vancouver, British Columbia, are established; (5) The President, Corporate Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer are appointed; (6) All filings, including the Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles, are confirmed and ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services (BC Online) via the Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name search through BC Online or an authorized service provider to verify name distinguishability. Submit a Name Reservation Request with the proposed legal element such as 'Inc.' or 'Corp.' Upload the search report and pay the reservation fee.
required_dossiers: Corporate name search report showing no conflicting names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for resemblance, submit a revised Name Reservation Request within 30 days or request a registrar review under the BCCA name rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance (BC Online filing portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Incorporation Application, Notice of Articles, and Incorporation Agreement online. Designate the director(s), registered office, and records office. Pay the statutory fee by credit card; the system issues the Certificate of Incorporation electronically.
required_dossiers: Incorporation Agreement signed by the incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar queries the application, file a corrected application, provide a statutory declaration, or submit an explanatory letter within 30 days of the deficiency notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office and Records Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance; registered office address in British Columbia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Retain a physical registered office in BC and obtain written consent of the office holder. File any change of registered office before the effective date. Maintain the statutory records at the records office.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as registered office (Form 2)
Consent to act as records office (Form 3)
Lease agreement or occupancy authorization for the BC address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If consent is defective, file a corrected consent accompanied by an affidavit of explanation and pay the administrative correction fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors (internal governance; no government filing fee)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting, adopt the first board resolution, approve the share subscription, appoint officers, and resolve to open a corporate bank account with designated signing authorities. Issue share certificates and initialize the share register.
required_dossiers: Director identification documents and consent forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a financial institution rejects the banking package, provide certified copies of the Certificate of Incorporation and Notice of Articles, or adopt a supplementary resolution clarifying signing authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency — Business Registration Online and General Index System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation for a federal Business Number using the Certificate of Incorporation. Open GST/HST (unless the small-supplier exemption applies), payroll, and corporate income tax accounts, and register for import/export accounts if cross-border B2B transactions are anticipated.
required_dossiers: Directors' personal identifiers (SIN or passport for non-residents)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA requests additional security or documentation, respond within 21 days with the prescribed forms and a supporting corporate resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Extra-Provincial Registration and Municipal Business Licence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance (if federal incorporation); local municipality (e.g., City of Vancouver Licensing Department)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the corporation was incorporated federally, file an extra-provincial registration in BC. If a physical office or warehouse will operate, obtain the applicable municipal business licence and confirm zoning compliance for the e-commerce administrative use.
required_dossiers: Notice of Articles or registered office evidence
Lease agreement and municipal zoning certificate
Fire safety inspection report (if premises occupied)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality conditions the licence on zoning or inspection, submit the outstanding inspection report, revised floor plan, or zoning interpretation letter within 10 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial manufacturing licensing board for electronic B2B platform operation; policy oversight by the Ministry of Jobs, Economic Development and Innovation (BC)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no industrial operating or manufacturing permit required; only a general municipal business licence if a physical office is occupied

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy, British Columbia (Environmental Assessment Office)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — service-only B2B platform without physical manufacturing or a stationary facility; no Environmental Assessment Certificate required under the Environmental Assessment Act, S.B.C. 2018, c. 8
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — no wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste streams generated; any office solid waste must comply with the Environmental Management Act, S.B.C. 2003, c. 53 and municipal waste bylaws

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and BC Building Code occupancy inspection for any leased office; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety clearance if employees are present; no industrial fire or civil defense permit required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) - federal corporate income tax (Part I), Part XIII withholding, and GST/HST administration. Integrated portal: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html) and Business Registration Online (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/registering-your-business/register-options.html). Provincial counterpart for British Columbia: BC Ministry of Finance, Consumer Taxation Branch (Provincial Sales Tax / PST) via eTaxBC portal (https://etax.gov.bc.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the federal/provincial business corporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the BC Business Corporations Act; if a federal CBCA corporation carries on business in BC, file an Extraprovincial Registration with the BC Registrar of Companies via Corporate Online / OneStop Business Registry. Step 2: Procure the federal Business Number (BN) and GST/HST program account through CRA Business Registration Online (BRO); non-resident applicants without a Canadian mailing address must appoint a resident representative (Form RC59) and may paper-file. Step 3: Register as a PST vendor with BC Consumer Taxation Branch via eTaxBC / OneStop; there is no monetary threshold for PST, and BC marketplace facilitator rules may deem the platform to be the vendor for facilitated taxable sales in BC. Step 4: If employing staff, register for CRA Payroll (RP) account, BC WorksafeBC, and applicable provincial employer accounts. Step 5: Coordinate the TIN equivalents: BN / RT0001 corporate income tax program account and RT0001 GST/HST account; for non-resident corporations earning only Canadian-source passive income, evaluate Part XIII withholding registration and any required section 116 certificate for dispositions of taxable Canadian property.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Canadian federal/provincial business corporation is a separate taxpayer under Part I of the Income Tax Act. A resident corporation (central management and control situated in Canada) is taxed on worldwide income; a non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada is taxed on Canadian-source business income under ss. 2(3) and 115, with additional Part XIV branch tax of 25% (treaty-reduced where applicable). The foreign affiliate regime (ss. 95-113) applies at entity level, providing exempt-surplus treatment for active foreign business income. No pass-through eligibility exists for corporations. Territorial scope for indirect tax: B2B cross-border wholesale platform services (ISIC 4791 / NAICS 425120) are generally zero-rated for GST/HST when supplied to non-residents, while domestic Canadian sales attract 5% GST and BC PST as applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box regime. Available statutory and treaty elections relevant to entity classification and hybrid/mismatch arrangements include: (a) treaty transparent-entity recognition for US LLCs and comparable fiscally transparent foreign entities under Canada-US Treaty Article IV(6) and analogous treaty provisions; (b) hybrid mismatch limitation rules under ss. 18.4-18.6, 94-94.4 of the Income Tax Act, which constrain deduction outcomes and require substantiated factual classification of offshore entities; (c) section 216 election permitting non-residents with Canadian rental income to compute net Part I tax instead of Part XIII gross withholding; (d) section 219(3) elective branch-tax base adjustments for non-resident corporations with Canadian branches; (e) GST/HST section 191 election for closely related corporations, deeming intercorporate taxable supplies to be made for nil consideration; (f) elections respecting foreign affiliate surplus/profit entitlement designations under s. 113 and Income Tax Regulations 5900-5907.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal value-added tax) plus British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST, a separate retail sales tax). Federal GST headline rate 5%; BC PST at 7% applies to most taxable BC consumer sales for a combined nominal exposure of 12% on domestic BC sales. B2B cross-border exports and offshore digital platform services are zero-rated for GST/HST and generally PST-exempt.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: CAD $30,000 in total worldwide taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated exports) measured over four consecutive calendar quarters; once exceeded, mandatory registration, collection, and remittance are required; voluntary registration is permitted for export-oriented businesses. BC PST: no general monetary threshold; vendor registration is due within 30 days of the first taxable sale in BC, and marketplace facilitator rules impose deemed-vendor obligations on cross-border e-commerce platforms facilitating taxable BC sales. BC PST registration is required for this entity only to the extent of tangible personal property or software supplied to BC end-consumers; pure B2B exports to non-residents remain zero-rated and PST-exempt.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, or digital stamping. CRA accepts standard electronic invoices (PDF, EDI, PEPPOL-based exchange) without prior clearance or approval; the Pan-Canadian Trust Framework is voluntary. GST/HST registrants must file returns electronically (GST/HST NETFILE is mandatory for registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD $1,500,000; others may paper-file). Records must be retained for six years in an electronically readable and readily accessible format with a preserved audit trail. BC PST returns are filed electronically via eTaxBC; no fiscal invoice clearance or cryptographic stamping requirements apply.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For a B2B cross-border wholesale marketplace (ISIC 4791 / NAICS 425120) operating from Canada: (1) services supplied to a non-resident (platform access, listing fees, transaction commissions, data services) are zero-rated under Excise Tax Act s. 23(1) provided the supply is not in respect of real property in Canada, goods situated in Canada at the time of supply, or a service rendered to an individual present in Canada; (2) digital and remote services supplied to non-residents are zero-rated under ETA s. 23.1; (3) tangible goods sold through the platform and exported from Canada are zero-rated under Schedule VI Part V (supply of goods delivered outside Canada) where export documentation is retained; (4) the place-of-supply rules (ETA ss. 13-23.1 and Selected Listed Financial Institution / VBE Rules) govern Canadian nexus; (5) the exporter must hold contemporaneous evidence of non-resident recipient status and physical movement of goods or offshore provision of services; zero-rated exporters retain full input tax credit recovery.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Canadian Export Declaration (CAED/GTR) or electronically filed export report for goods exceeding CAD $2,000 in value or for controlled/prohibited goods
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / cargo receipt evidencing export from Canada and delivery to a foreign destination
Commercial invoice, purchase order, and B2B platform contract identifying the non-resident customer and supply terms
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 credit advice or other bank proof of receipt of funds from abroad
Place-of-supply analysis memorandum under ETA ss. 13-23.1 and VBE Regulations documenting non-resident status of the recipient and the offshore supply analysis
Non-resident status attestation (certificate of residence or treaty residency declaration) collected from marketplace merchants
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may deny zero-rating, claw back previously allowed input tax credits, and reassess GST/HST at 5% (or 12% where BC HST/PST interaction applies) if export substantiation is deficient. Default reassessment window is four years under ETA s. 298; the period is unlimited where misrepresentation, neglect, or wilful default is established. Penalties: 50% of any false refund claimed under ETA s. 285.1; gross negligence penalty equal to the greater of CAD $250 and 25% of the tax under ETA s. 285; daily compound interest on unremitted amounts at the prescribed rate plus 2% under ETA s. 280; criminal prosecution for wilful evasion under ETA s. 327 carrying fines up to CAD $100,000 on indictment and possible imprisonment. Additional provincial exposure may arise if BC PST was improperly claimed as exempt or zero-rated; directors and officers may be liable for corporate GST/PST debts in cases of gross negligence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registry Services (BC Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two calendar months after each anniversary of the company's incorporation date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No immediate monetary penalty; continued failure for five consecutive years permits the registrar to administratively strike-off the company under BCBCA, requiring a formal restoration application and additional prescribed fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Information Return (federal corporate income tax filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty is 5% of the unpaid tax balance plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months for a first offence; repeated non-filing attracts a 10% base penalty plus 2% monthly. Compound daily interest also applies to outstanding balances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (applicable if the B2B marketplace is registered for GST/HST; registration is mandatory if taxable sales exceed CAD 30,000 in a consecutive 12-month period)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For annual filers, within three months after the corporation's fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file carries a penalty of 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per month up to 12 months; repeated failures raise the penalty. Daily compound interest applies to late remittances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (Corporations Canada) — required only for companies incorporated federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Repeated failure to file may lead to dissolution of the corporation by Corporations Canada; reinstatement requires payment of outstanding fees and a formal application.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the BC Business Corporations Act, there is no size-based monetary threshold. A company must appoint an auditor at each annual general meeting unless all shareholders entitled to vote execute a written resolution waiving the appointment for that fiscal year (section 196). This B2B marketplace may therefore avoid a statutory audit only through unanimous shareholder consent.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Private enterprises in Canada may elect either International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE). Publicly accountable corporations must use IFRS. For a private B2B platform corporation, the governing framework will be either IFRS or ASPE, as adopted in the first set of financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: BC private companies must maintain a transparency register of all significant individuals with significant control. The register must be updated within 30 days of any change, including share transfers that affect beneficial control. Although no public annual UBO filing is currently required in BC, the register must be actively maintained and available for inspection by the company and its members. Annual confirmation is typically completed alongside the annual general meeting or board review. Failure to maintain an accurate transparency register is an offense under the BCBCA.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 100 - 250 per year (CAD 135 - 340) for registered office and records-keeping services in British Columbia, depending on service scope and provider location.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - 25,000 per year for a certified independent audit of a private B2B platform corporation, depending on transaction volume, inter-company structures, and cross-border operations; audit may be waived by unanimous shareholder resolution.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined (15% federal general rate after s. 124 abatement and 13% general rate reduction; 12% BC general corporate income tax rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction: 9% federal + 2% BC on the first C$500,000 of active business income for CCPCs (combined 11%); SR&ED refundable ITCs up to 35% for CCPCs; 10% investment tax credit for eligible? ...
